# The Interrogation

---

The fluorescent light above the table buzzed with a faint electrical hum. Detective Maren Cole leaned back in her chair, arms crossed, watching the man across from her.

Marcus Webb. Thirty-four. Former employee of the victim. No priors.

She'd been at this for forty minutes.

"Mr. Webb." She let the name hang. "I need you to understand something. We don't arrest people without being sure."

Marcus's hands sat flat on the table, fingers splayed. She noticed how he kept adjusting his wedding ring. Twisting it. A nervous habit—or guilt. Hard to tell the difference in this light.

"I know," he said. Too quick. "I understand. I just—I don't know what else I can say. I already told the first officer everything."

"You told him what you want us to hear."

His jaw tightened. "That's not—that's not fair."

Maren opened the folder in front of her, though she'd long since memorized its emptiness. "We have the security footage from the loading dock. We have the timecard records. And we have your fingerprints on the door to Mr. Aldridge's office."

She watched his face. Nothing. But his foot started bouncing under the table—rapid, uncontrolled.

"The fingerprints don't mean anything," he said. "I was in that office every day. For two years."

"You were terminated three weeks ago."

"Yes." He swallowed. "Yes, I was."

"And yet there you were. The night he died."

Marcus's eyes darted to the two-way mirror, then back. "I didn't—I wasn't there to hurt anyone. I just needed to talk to him. About my severance. About the insurance. My wife, she's—" He stopped. Pressed his lips together. "I shouldn't have gone back. I know that. But I didn't do anything. I swear to God."

Maren uncrossed her arms and leaned forward. "Mr. Webb. We have witnesses who saw someone matching your description near the building at eleven-forty. The coroner puts time of death between eleven and midnight."

"I told you—I was there at eleven-thirty. I was in and out in ten minutes. I didn't even see him. His office was dark."

"So you admit you were there."

"I—" He exhaled sharply. "Why are you doing this? Why won't you just tell me what you want me to say?"
